# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82 (Bu-Vb Pc82)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pariṇāmana-sikkhāpada* is the eighty-second rule in the Pācittiya section of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a monk incurs an offense requiring confession if he knowingly diverts to an individual an offering or gain (*lābha*) that had been dedicated to the monastic community (*saṅgha*) [SuttaCentral; Dutt 1924; Stache-Rosen 1984]. Sukumar Dutt notes that this rule legally precluded individual appropriation of Saṅgha-dedicated property, restricting monastic members strictly to usufruct rights rather than individual ownership [Dutt 1924]. Ute Hüsken similarly highlights that Pācittiya 82, together with Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30, strictly regulates and prohibits the diversion of goods destined for the community to an individual [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pācittiya 82), the Parivāra (Pācittiya 82), and the parallel nun's rule in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pācittiya 160) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other Vinaya traditions are found in the Mahīśāsaka and Mahāsāṅghika Vinayas (both Chinese and Sanskrit recensions), the Lokottaravādin Bhikṣu- and Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣas, and the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchāsūtra* (Pācittiya 10) [SuttaCentral; Stache-Rosen 1984]. At the passage level, SuttaCentral notes a close relationship with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30 [SuttaCentral]. This is strongly corroborated by DharmaNexus, which computes its closest internal text-reuse with Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30 (6 matches, spanning §1.1–2.1.12 to §1.1–2.13 with 0.88 similarity), among 373 matching passages across 87 Pali texts, alongside other Pācittiya rules and the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text with Tibetan canonical Vinaya commentaries, notably the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) and the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].
